sources.citation: Arenz, Karl; Barros, Cândida; Gauz, Valeria. 2019. Um Catecismo Amazônico: O "Compendio da Doutrina Christam na Língua Portugueza & Brasilica" de João Felipe Bettendorff (1687). Anthropos 114(1): 181-194.
sources.note: no phonology content; the 2019 specialists on Bettendorff's manuscripts report no surviving text of the Urucucu dialogue.

sources.citation: Harris, Mark. 2015. Sistemas regionais, relações interétnicas e movimentos territoriais – os Tapajó e além na história ameríndia. Revista de Antropologia (São Paulo) 58(1): 33-68. doi:10.11606/2179-0892.ra.2015.102099
sources.note: No phonology content. Language remarks are generic: the Lower Amazon formations were multilingual (pp. 37-38: 'seria imprudente afirmar que um grupo falasse uma única língua'; likely Tupi-Guarani, Karib and Arawak present), the Tapajó were non-Tupi (p. 43), Heriarte's 'differentes lingoas'. No word of Urucucú (or of Tapajó beyond one kin term) is given; nothing on stress or tone.

sources.note: Nothing. Mission history/biography; no indigenous-language material at all (the only language content is Bettendorff's own six European languages, his learning of the língua geral, and his 1687 Portuguese-Tupi Compendio). a full-text search for stress/accent acento/tônic/tonal/sílaba/prosód/fonolog/fonétic: 0 relevant ('acentuada' once = 'more marked hostility').

sources.citation: Menéndez, Miguel A. 1981/1982. Uma contribuição para a etno-história da área Tapajós-Madeira. Revista do Museu Paulista, Nova Série 28: 289-388, 9 quadros, 11 mapas.
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnohistorical compilation; the only content on the languoid is its listing among Tapajós-river groups and (p. 312) 'Quanto aos Orurucú, que Heriarte indica como vizinhos dos Tapajó, a existência e localização desse grupo parecem ser confirmadas pelo fato de Betendorf escrever catecismos na língua dos Tapajó e dos Ururucú, dando a entender que contingentes deste grupo também se encontravam na aldeia daqueles.' Not one word of the language; no affiliation proposed; a full-text search for stress/accent the whole scanned text for acento/acentua/tônic/tonal/sílaba/prosód/fonolog/fonétic…

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1952. The Tapajó. Translated and edited by John Howland Rowe. Kroeber Anthropological Society Papers 6: 1-25.
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic paper; 'Language' paragraph (p. 6) says only that neither tribe at the Tapajós mouth spoke Tupi, that Bettendorff translated the catechism into the Urucucú language (translation lost) and that Heriarte said the Orucucuzes spoke a language distinct from the Tupinambaranas'. Not one Urucucú word is recorded; no phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Bettendorff, João Filipe. 1910 [1698]. Chronica da Missão dos Padres da Companhia de Jesus no Estado do Maranhão. Revista do Instituto Historico e Geographico Brazileiro 72(1): 1-697.
sources.note: The 17th-century primary source for the existence of the Urucucú language (p. 168 says the catechism was translated into it). Nimuendajú states it gives no linguistic data on Urucucú; worth a single check only to confirm that no word or remark on the language survives. Cannot contain a stress statement in any modern sense.
sources.venue: Revista do Instituto Historico e Geographico Brazileiro

sources.citation: Heriarte, Maurício de. 1874 [1662]. Descripção do Estado do Maranhão, Pará, Corupá e Rio das Amazonas. Vienna: Carlos Gerold. (pp. 35-39 on the Tapajós and Orucucuzes)
sources.note: Second 17th-century witness cited by Nimuendajú for the Orucucuzes speaking a language distinct from Lingua Geral; only three Tapajó proper names survive from it and no Urucucú words. Confirmation of 'unattested' status only.
sources.venue: Descripção do Estado do Maranhão, Pará, Corupá e Rio das Amazonas
